paragraphs.source_en: How successful are fund choices based on the number of stars awarded for such short-term achievements? Not very! According to a 2014 study by the *Wall Street Journal*, only 14 percent of five-star funds in 2004 still held that rating a decade later. Approximately 36 percent of those original five-star funds dropped one star, and the remaining 50 percent dropped to three or fewer stars. Yes, fund performance reverts toward the mean, or even below.

paragraphs.source_en: If it were easy to select funds that would outperform their peers by simply buying yesterday’s winners, we would expect to see persistence; that is, most funds that ended the first period at the top of the heap would remain there in the next period and those at the bottom would remain there. But no. As it turns out, RTM overpowers persistence.
